title: U.S. public-health protection depends on operational capacity that funding totals alone do not guarantee
source_unit: Trust for America’s Health, Underfunded and Under Strain: The State of America’s Public Health System, September 2026; policy analysis of federal, state, and local public-health funding, workforce, infrastructure, and operations
geography: United States; federal public-health system with state, local, territorial, and community implications

denominator.unit: report-defined U.S. public-health system and national health-expenditure estimates

government_public_health_share_of_health.unit: percent of $5.3 trillion U.S. health expenditures in 2024

cdc_program_funding_fy2026.unit: billion dollars; approximately flat with FY2025

cdc_per_capita_purchasing_power_change.unit: percent change from approximately $30.30 to $26.71 in constant dollars per person

observations.method: TFAH policy analysis of national health expenditures, federal appropriations, inflation-adjusted funding, and per-capita purchasing power using cited government and research sources.
observations.uncertainty: The report is a nonprofit policy analysis and its funding comparisons depend on definitions, inflation adjustments, program boundaries, and cited-source revisions; spending shares do not directly measure service quality or health outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Federal, state, local, territorial, and community public-health systems and the populations they serve.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small public-health share of total health spending may reflect the boundary between governmental prevention and clinical care; nominal funding stability can coexist with capacity loss, but the report does not estimate a single causal effect on population health.

observations.method: TFAH synthesis of Office of Personnel Management and agency workforce information cited in the report.
observations.uncertainty: Workforce counts vary by date, agency definition, personnel category, and treatment of separations or rescinded actions; headcount change does not itself measure productivity, service quality, or whether capacity was replaced elsewhere.
observations.subgroup: Federal health agencies and the state, local, and community programs dependent on their technical, grant, surveillance, and emergency functions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A smaller workforce could reflect restructuring or changed mission scope, but the report argues that the reductions occurred while demands and responsibilities remained high; the causal consequences remain context-specific.

observations.period: 2021–2025; public-health workforce and local capacity baseline

denominator.unit: report-cited public-health workforce and local-health-department estimates

estimated_state_local_staffing_gap.unit: additional full-time-equivalent positions estimated as a minimum baseline need

workforce_burnout_symptoms.unit: percent of 2024 PH WINS respondents reporting at least one burnout symptom

epidemiologists_planning_to_leave.unit: percent planning to leave their agency within one year

local_health_departments_budget_cuts.value: 17 experienced in FY2024; 23 anticipated in FY2025

observations.method: TFAH synthesis of cited workforce surveys and local-health-department capacity studies; estimates come from different sources and denominators.
observations.uncertainty: The measures are not a single survey or common denominator; the 80,000-position estimate is a baseline staffing study, while burnout, turnover, and budget measures come from distinct instruments and periods.
observations.subgroup: State and local public-health workers, epidemiologists, and local health departments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Burnout and turnover intentions do not guarantee departure; staffing gaps can be partly mitigated by technology, partnerships, or changed service models, though those substitutions may create new fragility.

denominator.unit: report-defined public-health programs and operational functions

funding_capacity_gap.value: appropriated dollars are necessary but not sufficient
funding_capacity_gap.unit: report synthesis linking staffing, grant administration, technical assistance, data systems, and timely disbursement to program function

grant_disruption.value: more than $12 billion in federal grants accessed for termination or clawback before later litigation and partial relief

operational_margin.unit: report synthesis of temporary funding, expiring positions, workforce strain, and fragmented infrastructure

observations.method: TFAH policy analysis of federal actions, appropriations, grant operations, workforce, technical assistance, and front-line interviews with state and local health officials.
observations.uncertainty: The report is an advocacy-oriented synthesis and documents disruption through cited sources and interviews; it does not provide a standardized national measure of program performance or attribute each community outcome to a specific administrative action.
observations.subgroup: Public-health agencies, grantees, community organizations, and populations relying on surveillance, prevention, preparedness, and response functions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some disruptions may be temporary, litigated, or offset by state and local action; operational uncertainty itself can reduce planning capacity even when nominal funding later returns.

denominator.unit: report analysis of the FY2027 President's Budget Request

proposed_resources_reduction_for_cdc_and.unit: billion dollars; approximately 31% reduction relative to FY2026 after accounting for proposed transfers

prevention_public_health_fund.unit: reported policy proposal; not enacted outcome

threats_named_by_report.value: measles, declining childhood vaccination, foodborne outbreaks, extreme heat, overdose, suicide, and emergency preparedness needs

observations.method: TFAH analysis of the FY2027 budget proposal and comparison with FY2026 enacted funding; recommendations and policy projections are kept separate from enacted facts.
observations.uncertainty: The budget request is a proposal and may be amended, rejected, or offset; reported resource changes are not realized cuts, and the report’s policy interpretation reflects TFAH’s advocacy position.
observations.subgroup: Federal, state, local, territorial, and community public-health capabilities and the populations exposed to preventable health threats.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reorganization or redistribution could preserve some functions despite aggregate reductions, though the report argues that specialized expertise, continuity, and foundational capacity are difficult to replace quickly.

related_sources.claim: Full 140-page issue report with cited funding, workforce, operational, front-line, and budget evidence.

boundary: This record captures TFAH’s evidence and policy analysis of U.S. public-health funding, workforce, infrastructure, operational continuity, and proposed federal changes. It does not establish a causal national health effect, independently audit every cited estimate, measure all state or local variation, or treat proposed FY2027 policy as enacted fact.
